title: Getting started
summary: Find your way around MessageMonkey and choose the right starting point.
topics:
MessageMonkey is MOED’s email and audience workspace. Use it to organize connections, create campaigns, collect signups and survey responses, run automations, and review results. Each account has one shared audience. Check the account banner before making changes.

A MessageMonkey connection is an audience record with an email status, tags, and profile fields. Do not assume that editing an audience record also updates an organization or contact elsewhere in MOED.

Start at Home for a snapshot of activity. For a first campaign, review your connections, prepare your content, and check delivery setup before sending.

The sidebar opens Campaigns, Automations, Forms, Audience, Content, Analytics, and the AI tools available to your role. Related pages appear beneath the active area. The sidebar control minimizes navigation; on a small screen, use the menu button to open it.

Use Search MessageMonkey in the top bar to find available pages, connections, campaigns, flows, and help. Use each page’s search box for that list. Theme controls in the account tools switch between light and dark display.

Return here through User Manual. Search this guide with words such as “import”, “unsubscribe”, or “schedule”. Press / to focus the manual search, Enter to open the first matching topic, and Escape in the search field to clear it.

Search, filters, sorting, and pagination work together. If an item seems missing, clear the filters and check the archived or removed view. The page arrows move through the current result set; the page-size control changes how many rows you see.

Before a bulk action, read the selection count and scope. Selected rows and all matching results are different scopes. Hover over an action icon, or focus it with the keyboard, to read its label. Forms, Surveys, and Automations show Results before Edit.

Action icons gain a background on hover or focus. An orange outline that remains visible indicates an action protected by Admin Unlock. The outline is a permission cue; it does not mean the action has already run.

title: Roles and protected actions
summary: Understand which tools are available and how confirmation protects important changes.
topics:
Common role permissions
RoleWhat you can do
ReviewerBrowse permitted audience records, campaigns, forms, automations, and reports; use Ask Analytics AI and this manual. Editing, imports, exports, Inbox, and Write with AI require an editor or administrator.
EditorCreate and edit content, manage audience records, use imports and exports, and work in Inbox. Sending also requires unrestricted access and successful delivery checks.
AdministratorUse editor tools plus administrative delivery settings and protected deletion or cleanup actions. Some actions also require a recent Admin Unlock.

Demo restrictions, account security requirements, and role preview can further limit these capabilities. A role name alone does not guarantee that sending or account configuration is available.

An orange outline marks a control that needs Admin Unlock. An administrator must complete the unlock prompt before the protected operation can proceed. If an unlock expires, complete it again when prompted.

Unlocking does not replace the action’s confirmation. Read the item name, count, and consequences before confirming. If a dialog requests a particular word, type that word exactly. Do not use permanent deletion when archiving or removing an item from a list would meet your need.

Use the page’s Save or Save draft control and wait for the saved confirmation. A preview, AI suggestion, or open editor is not proof that a change has been saved.

If MessageMonkey says a record changed, another save may have happened since you opened it. Preserve your unsaved text, reload the current record, compare the changes, and apply what is still needed. Repeatedly submitting an old screen will not resolve a version conflict.

title: Connections, imports, and exports
summary: Maintain accurate audience profiles and move data with the correct scope.
topics:
1. Open Audience. Choose Add connections → Add a single connection, or open an existing connection.
  2. Enter or review the email address, name, profile fields, and email subscription status. Use the person’s actual consent when choosing a status.
  3. Add relevant tags and groups. Use notes for useful context that does not belong in a structured field.
  4. Save, then review the profile and its activity. For multiple records, filter the list and check the selection before applying a bulk change.

Custom fields and merge tags are managed from the audience menu. Required fields and validation messages must be resolved before saving.

A connection's email status describes its permission or ability to receive campaign email. Having an audience record, tag, or group membership does not by itself give permission to send.

Audience member email statuses
StatusWhat it meansEmail eligibility and next steps
SubscribedPermission to receive campaign email has been recorded.May receive campaigns and automation emails when active, selected, and otherwise eligible. This status does not guarantee delivery.
UnsubscribedThe person has opted out of campaign email, or the record was explicitly marked unsubscribed.Excluded from campaign email. A public signup must complete a fresh email confirmation before this address can rejoin, even on a single opt-in form.
Non-subscribedThe audience record exists, but permission to receive campaign email has not been obtained or recorded. This is different from an opt-out.Excluded from campaign email. Obtain and record permission, or have the person subscribe through a signup form, before treating them as subscribed.
CleanedThe address has been identified as invalid or undeliverable, such as after a permanent bounce.Excluded from campaign email. Supply a corrected address and fresh permission before subscribing it. Changing the status or repeating a signup cannot clear the block on the same address.

Pending is an additional confirmation state: a double opt-in signup is awaiting email confirmation and is not yet subscribed. Confirmation and delivery events control Pending and Cleaned; do not use a status change to bypass either safeguard.

Non-subscribed versus Unsubscribed: both are excluded from campaign email, but Non-subscribed means permission is missing, while Unsubscribed records an opt-out. Importing a record or adding a tag does not supply missing permission.

Archiving removes a connection from the active audience view while retaining its record and email status. Find it under Archived connections to review or restore it. Restoring a record does not create new consent or clear an email suppression.

Permanent deletion is different from unsubscribing and requires an administrator, a recent Admin Unlock, and the requested typed confirmation. Use Unsubscribe to honor an opt-out.

1. Choose Add connections → Import connections and upload a file accepted by the import screen.
  2. Map columns to email, names, custom fields, groups, or tags. Inspect the preview instead of relying only on column names.
  3. Review subscription status, existing-record handling, and the target tags or groups. Confirm that the source supports the intended email permissions.
  4. Start the import. Follow its progress in the job view or Import history.
  5. Read the completion summary and row errors. Correct rejected data and verify a few imported profiles before using the audience in a campaign.

A queued or partially processed job is not a completed import. Use the available job controls to resume or cancel as appropriate. Import undo is a protected operation: read its stated scope before confirming, especially if records have since been edited.

Editors and administrators can export permitted data. Set the desired filters, choose the export scope, and confirm whether the export contains selected connections or the complete matching set. A single connection also has an Export action on its profile.

Open Export history from the audience menu to review progress and download completed jobs. Check the file contents and any included supporting files before sharing them. Keep exports only where the people receiving them are allowed to access the audience data.

title: Tags, groups, fields, and segments
summary: Choose the right way to organize connections and target a message.
topics:
Tags are labels you apply to connections, such as a volunteer team or event interest. Open Audience → Tags to create or rename a tag. Click the tag’s name to see its connections; a separate View connections action is unnecessary.

Apply tags from a profile, a selected audience list, the bulk-tag tool, or an import. Removing a tag from a connection changes that association. Deleting a tag definition removes the label and its associations while keeping the connections; protected deletion requires the access shown by the control.

Groups organize choices within a category, such as areas of interest. Choose the group’s display type and options to fit the question. When exposed in a signup or preferences form, these choices can be selected by the subscriber.

Fields hold structured values such as a name, date, address, or number. In Fields and merge tags, choose the correct field type, required setting, public visibility, and any default value. Treat removing a field or group option as a data change, not just a visual adjustment.

Use the field’s merge tag to personalize content. Preview messages with representative records, including one with a blank optional field, so missing data does not produce an awkward greeting or broken link.

1. Open Audience → Segments and create a segment.
  2. Add rules for the available profile, membership, activity, or engagement criteria.
  3. Choose whether connections must match all rules or any rule. Review the resulting connections and count.
  4. Save the segment with a name that explains its purpose, then use it when selecting a campaign audience.

A segment describes criteria, so membership can change as records and activity change. Recheck the campaign’s recipient review near send time. A match is not a promise of delivery: unsubscribes, suppressions, and other sending checks still apply.

title: Campaigns and planning
summary: Move from an idea to a complete email draft and an organized campaign plan.
topics:
1. Choose Create Campaign and select the available email type. Give the draft an internal name you can recognize later.
  2. Complete the recipient selection, sender details, subject, and preview text. Review any exclusions.
  3. Choose or create the email content. Save your edits before returning to the campaign checklist.
  4. Review settings and tracking, preview the email, and send an appropriate test when delivery access allows it.
  5. Use Finish later to return to the campaign list, or continue to the separate send review when the draft is ready.

Saving a campaign does not send it. The final sending or scheduling step is separate and performs its own readiness checks.

Use the Campaigns search, filters, folders, and status views to find the right email. Open its name to review it. A duplicate is a starting point for a new message; recheck recipients, dates, sender information, links, and subject before sending.

Archive campaigns you want out of the active list while retaining their history. Review archived items before restoring or permanently deleting anything. If an email has already been sent, changing a new draft cannot change the copy in recipients’ inboxes.

Campaign Manager groups planned work around a campaign. Create a campaign plan, then add touchpoints for the messages and activities that belong to it. Use the available calendar and list views to review timing and open a touchpoint to adjust its details.

A planning date helps coordinate work. Confirm the linked email’s actual send or schedule status separately. Before an event date changes, review all affected touchpoints and scheduled emails instead of assuming one edit updates every message.

title: Email templates and the editor
summary: Build reusable emails and check how the final message will read.
topics:
Open Campaigns → Email templates to browse saved designs or start a new one. Choose a starter that fits the message, then replace example text, links, and images. Organize reusable designs with clear names and folders.

Saving a template makes it available for future work; it does not send an email. A campaign using a template still needs its own content review and recipient settings. After changing a reusable template, check an existing campaign directly rather than assuming its draft has changed too.

1. Select a content block to edit its text, image, button, or other supported content.
  2. Use the block and style controls for spacing, alignment, colors, and typography. Keep button labels short and descriptive.
  3. Insert approved files and logos from Content. Add useful image descriptions and check every destination URL.
  4. Use Undo and Redo to correct recent edits, then Save. Review the saved state before leaving the editor.

Keep essential information in text as well as images. Include a meaningful link label, such as “View the event details”, so the message remains understandable when images are blocked.

Review desktop and mobile previews, the plain-text content where available, and the final subject and preview text. Check merge tags with realistic connection values and missing optional values. Confirm dates, names, amounts, contact information, and unsubscribe or preferences links.

Send a test through the provided test-email control when allowed, then inspect the actual received email and click its links. A visual preview does not prove that sender setup or delivery is working. Resolve any test or preflight error before attempting the real send.

title: Content and Brand Kit
summary: Keep images, files, and brand choices ready for consistent messages.
topics:
Open Content → My files to upload supported assets and organize them into folders. Choose a descriptive filename and inspect the uploaded result. Search or filter the library when selecting content for an email or form.

When an image-editing control is available, check the crop and dimensions in the destination layout. Avoid embedding important text only inside an image. Before removing a file, consider where it is already used: recipients may open older messages long after they were sent.

Use Content → Brand Kit to manage the logos, colors, and font choices offered by MessageMonkey. Review a logo against both light and dark backgrounds and choose colors with enough contrast for readable text and controls.

Save the brand choices, then inspect them in the email or form you are building. Brand settings help you stay consistent, but each design still needs a preview. Verify the final appearance instead of assuming a brand update has revised every previously saved item.

title: Delivery, sending, and scheduling
summary: Check readiness, approve the final audience, and follow delivery outcomes.
topics:
An unrestricted administrator configures Campaigns → Email delivery. Follow the setup screen for the Amazon SES sending identity, domain authentication, event notifications, and public email links. Complete the displayed verification steps and review readiness results.

Use an address and domain the account is authorized to send from. If verification is pending or a delivery requirement fails, fix that requirement before sending. Inbox receiving sources have their own setup; a working outgoing sender does not by itself establish an inbound route.

1. Open the saved campaign and complete its checklist. Recheck the recipients and exclusions, sender, reply address, subject, and content.
  2. Run the available review and test tools. Resolve blockers and understand any warnings.
  3. Choose Send or the scheduling option. Review the final recipient count and the date, time, and time zone displayed by the scheduling screen.
  4. Complete the final confirmation. Wait for the success or queued result before leaving the page.
  5. Open the delivery view to confirm the campaign’s actual state and progress.

Sending requires an unrestricted editor or administrator, suitable account security access, and successful readiness checks. A saved draft or planning touchpoint is not a scheduled send.

Queued means work is waiting to be processed. Provider acceptance is different from confirmed delivery. Delivery events can include delivered messages, bounces, complaints, and other failures. Read the campaign’s delivery details to understand which stage has been reached.

Unsubscribed, cleaned, archived, or suppressed connections may be excluded from a send. Do not change status simply to force delivery. Investigate the reason, correct bad data when appropriate, and obtain valid permission where needed.

If sending appears stalled, check the current delivery state and error details before retrying. A repeat confirmation or a duplicate campaign can create a second send; first establish what the original operation actually did.

title: Automations
summary: Build a flow, review its rules, and monitor what happens to enrolled connections.
topics:
1. Open Automations and choose a flow template or Build from scratch.
  2. Configure the entry trigger and the available conditions, delays, and actions. Read each step’s description; a template still needs your account’s choices.
  3. Review every email and recipient condition. Check for missing values, unintended branches, and delays that do not fit the intended timing.
  4. Save the flow, choose Continue, and resolve the validation issues before turning it on.

Keep a new flow in draft while reviewing it. Activating an email automation can lead to real sends when its trigger and conditions are met.

An active flow offers Pause & Edit. Pausing keeps connections’ positions while you review the flow. Save the changes, review them, and use Turn back on when ready.

Inspect the flow’s history and affected steps before changing timing or branching. Do not assume that a saved edit has already resumed a paused flow, or that it rewrites messages that have already been sent.

In the automation list, Results appears before Edit. Use Results to review the flow’s reported activity and execution outcomes. Investigate failed or waiting steps in context rather than treating every enrolled connection as a delivered email.

Archive a flow when it is no longer needed in the active list. Restoring an archived flow returns it as a draft so it can be reviewed before activation. Permanent deletion is a separate protected action. A duplicate also needs its own review before use.

title: Forms, surveys, and preferences
summary: Collect signups, gather feedback, and let connections manage their choices.
topics: Build and publish a signup form

1. Open Forms and choose the supported form type, such as hosted, embedded, or popup. Landing pages are available under Campaigns.
  2. Edit the fields, wording, styling, success message, and settings. Request only information you need and make the subscription purpose clear.
  3. Preview the form on desktop and mobile. Test required fields, validation, and the completion experience.
  4. Publish when ready, then use the public link or supplied embed instructions. Check the published version from the place where visitors will find it.

Saving a draft does not publish it. If confirmation or double opt-in is enabled, test the confirmation email and follow-up step too. A submission awaiting confirmation is not the same as a confirmed subscription.

Open Audience → Surveys, choose a starting point, and edit the questions and answer choices. Preview the complete survey before publishing and sharing its public link. Check whether the questions collect the information you actually need.

Forms and Surveys place the Results action before Edit. Open Results to inspect the available submissions, counts, and charts. Apply the report filters and date range before interpreting totals. Export controls require the appropriate role.

A form visit, a submission, and a confirmed signup are different events. Use the metric label and the resource’s settings to understand what a result represents.

Audience → Subscriber preferences controls the experience for updating the choices exposed to connections. Review the fields and groups presented there, then test the experience using a representative connection.

Changing preferences is different from unsubscribing. Keep the unsubscribe path available and understandable. Use the supported personalized links in messages rather than copying one person’s private preferences URL into a campaign for everyone.

Archive an unused form or survey to remove it from active work while preserving its results. Restoring a resource as a draft lets you review its content and settings before publishing again.

title: Inbox conversations
summary: Manage replies, drafts, and follow-up with individual connections.
topics:
Editors and administrators open Audience → Inbox. Use its navigation to review To do, Done, all conversations, Trash, drafts, and the available source or label filters.

An unrestricted administrator manages receiving sources. Follow the Sources setup and routing verification instructions, including an external test message when requested. Preparing a receiving address does not itself send that test. If replies are missing, verify the receiving route and filters before assuming the conversation was deleted.
Reply, save a draft, or add a note

1. Open the conversation and read the latest messages. Verify the connection and the intended recipient.
  2. Write a reply, optionally starting from a saved message template. Personalize its text and inspect links and attachments.
  3. Use Save draft to keep unfinished work, or Send reply after reviewing it. Sending requires unrestricted access and the necessary delivery readiness.
  4. Check the queued message and its delivery status in the conversation.

An internal note records context for your team; it is different from a reply to the connection. Check which composer mode you are using before saving or sending. Respect opt-outs and any send restrictions shown for the recipient.

Use labels to organize conversations and Mark done when follow-up is complete. Done is a workflow state, not deletion; find completed conversations through the Done or all-conversations view.

Use Trash only when you intend to remove a conversation from ordinary work. Check the available restore controls before considering permanent cleanup. Reusable message templates can be managed separately from the conversation drafts that use them.

title: Analytics and custom reports
summary: Read performance in context and save useful report definitions.
topics:
Start in Analytics and select the relevant dashboard or report. Set the date range, comparison period, message scope, and other available filters. Check the bot-activity setting when interpreting opens or clicks.

Email reports focus on message performance; Audience reports describe the audience; Conversion insights report the supported form or conversion activity. Recipient activity, link performance, locations and clients, and timing views answer more specific questions.

Read each metric’s label and denominator. A sent count differs from delivered messages, and a rate may use a different base from a nearby total. Mail privacy tools and automated link checks can affect engagement signals. An open or click is evidence of a recorded event, not proof that a person read the message.

1. Open Analytics → Custom reports and start a report if your role allows it.
  2. Choose the available dataset, metrics, grouping, and filters. Preview the resulting table or chart.
  3. Give the report a useful name and select the available visibility setting. Confirm whether it is private or shared.
  4. Save it and return to the report list. Use Search reports and Favorites only to find reports you use often.

Removed reports changes the list to removed entries; Clear all clears the search/filter controls. Check that view when a saved report seems missing. Removing a report definition is different from deleting the underlying campaign or connection records.

Use the same date range and filters when comparing reports. If two totals differ, first check message selection, dataset, bot filtering, and whether one result counts unique recipients while another counts events.

Editors and administrators can use available export controls. Include the report name, date range, filters, and metric definitions when sharing results so someone else can understand the numbers. Re-run the report when fresh delivery or engagement events may have arrived.

title: Ask Analytics AI and Write with AI
summary: Use AI for evidence-based questions and editable writing suggestions.
topics: Ask a question about your data

Open Ask Analytics AI from the sidebar or the relevant analytics context. Set the period and scope, then ask a specific question, such as which selected messages had the strongest click performance.

Read the answer alongside its supplied evidence and reporting context. Check unexpected figures in Analytics. If data is unavailable or too limited, narrow the question or choose a period with activity. An AI explanation does not establish causation or replace the underlying report.

1. Open Write with AI, available to editors and administrators.
  2. Choose the writing task and provide the text, purpose, audience, and tone that will help shape the result. A starter button can supply an initial prompt.
  3. Select Generate suggestions. Read the suggestions and choose the text you want to use.
  4. Use Check content when you want feedback, then make any needed changes in the actual draft.
  5. Review facts, dates, names, promises, links, and merge tags before saving or sending the final email.

The text you provide and basic brand context go to MOED’s configured AI service. Include only information appropriate for that task. Generated suggestions do not automatically send a campaign.

Use request history to revisit available earlier work. Give a new request enough context to stand on its own, especially when changing tasks or reporting scope.

If a request is taking too long, use Stop where offered and check its resulting state before retrying. If the AI service is unavailable, preserve your text and continue editing manually. A failed or interrupted response is not a completed content check.

title: Troubleshooting and common questions
summary: Resolve the most common problems without losing work or repeating a send.
topics: An item or action is missing

Confirm the account banner, search text, filters, page number, and selected status view. Look in Archived, Removed reports, or Trash as appropriate. If a control is missing, check your role and any role-preview or demo restrictions.

For a visible orange-outlined control, complete Admin Unlock using an administrator account. If access is still denied, report the exact action and error rather than trying a bookmarked administrative URL.
An email will not send or a reply is missing

Read the readiness or delivery error first. Check the sender identity, recipient eligibility, required content, public links, and account security restrictions. Ask an administrator to resolve delivery configuration issues.

For a campaign already submitted, inspect its delivery view before retrying. For an Inbox reply, inspect the conversation’s queued message and delivery state. For missing incoming mail, check Inbox sources and routing verification as well as conversation filters.
A save failed or the page changed

Copy valuable unsaved text before refreshing. Resolve any field validation message. If another user changed the record, reopen the latest version and reconcile your edits with it. If your session expired, sign in again before continuing.

When a long-running import or export appears stuck, review its job status and errors. Use the supported job controls instead of starting the same operation again without checking its progress.
A layout looks wrong or you need more help

Preview the affected email or form at both desktop and mobile sizes. Check image dimensions, long links, oversized text, and contrast in the chosen theme. For an email, compare the preview with an actual test message because email clients render designs differently.

When requesting help, provide the page or item name, the steps you took, the expected result, the exact error, and the time of the problem. Include your role and whether you were using a preview or demo session. A screenshot can help, but omit passwords, private tokens, and unnecessary connection data.
